svg.title: tandem architecture, one spec end to end
svg.desc: Animated: a planner submits a spec through the CLI and bridge; the supervisor starts an OpenCode session; the implementer model edits the working tree; events stream back over SSE; a protected-file permission request is escalated to a human, who denies it from a phone; the implementer finishes and the planner's wait returns the result.
svg.text: tandem serve: one process, one event loop

g.text: The planner submits a spec. The bridge hands it to the supervisor, which journals it.
POST /session, then /prompt_async. The marker makes delivery idempotent across restarts.
OpenCode drives the implementer model: reasoning, tool calls, more reasoning.
Edits land in the working tree
Meanwhile the supervisor hashes protected files to catch edits made another way.
The pump reads SSE /event, writes events.sse, and feeds the supervisor. The monitor times it.
The implementer wants to edit instruction.md
A per-session rule stops it. OpenCode waits for a human, with the diff attached.
Every alert goes to notifications.log; --notify-cmd or --ntfy-topic push it to you.
Level-triggered: the planner sees the blocked state, however late it calls wait.
Same client, same bridge, same journal: POST /permission/{id}/reply from your phone.
It writes results/S-1.json naming the active spec, written after the latest prompt.
Only now is the result read, so the planner never reviews a moving target.
The planner reads tandem result, then checks tandem diff instead of trusting it.
